facts.fact: Under the DGA Basic Agreement a Director is one who directs the production of motion pictures, as the word is commonly used in the industry.

A director's tasks include studying scripts to decide how to direct them, planning each shot's framing, composition, camera movement, sound and actor movement, supervising camera, lighting, design and sound crews, and holding auditions for parts.
During shooting the director sees the dailies of each day's photography at a reasonable time.

After photography the director prepares the Director's Cut for the individual producer and for the person the deal memo names as having final cutting authority; the deal memo, not the agreement, names who holds final cut.
On a theatrical feature and on a non-series television film of 90 minutes or longer the director has the right to select the First Assistant Director, consistent with the budget.

The DGA Basic Agreement covers directors, UPMs, ADs and associate directors in film and television, and its rate card sets separate minimums for theatrical features, network prime time, non-network television, basic cable, pay television and high-budget SVOD on services with 20 million or more subscribers.

A director of an episodic television episode works to a guaranteed preparation period and a guaranteed shooting period set by the episode length and medium, for example 7 prep days and 8 shooting days for a one-hour network prime-time episode.
Stage directing in the US is covered by the Stage Directors and Choreographers Society, a national labor union that covers stage work in the United States only.

The DGA assistant-director ladder most often followed is Second Assistant Director, then First Assistant Director, then Unit Production Manager; the training program says an assistant director is not a junior director or director-in-training.
A trainee or intern reaches the Southern California Second Assistant Directors' Qualification List after 400 days of on-the-job training, at least 75% of them with the shooting company.
A Second Assistant Director qualifies for the Southern California First Assistant Directors' list after 520 working days as a Second AD.
A First Assistant Director qualifies for the Southern California UPM list after 260 working days as a First AD.
The Los Angeles Assistant Directors Training Program takes 1.5 to 3.5 years to complete its 400 paid days; the New York program runs two full years with at least 350 production days.

Before directing a first episode of a dramatic or high-budget SVOD/AVOD series, a first-time director must attend the Guild's Television Director Orientation Course on Professional Standards for Episodic Directors.

On a 30 to 60 minute episodic program the employer may assign a Consulting Director to advise a director who has not directed under the BA before; the consultant gets no credit and no creative rights.

In the 2020-21 season employers gave 113 first episodic-directing jobs; 64% went to people already working on the show (mostly writer-producers and actors) and 36% to career-track directors, and two-thirds of career-track directors went on to direct another series against 25% of affiliated directors.
The DGA counted 382 first DGA-covered features released between 2018 and 2022.

A director joins the DGA by being hired by a signatory company to direct, or by making their own company or project signatory; an established director with acclaimed US theatrical features may occasionally be invited.

After the Guild receives a deal memo from a signatory employer, the applicant is sent an application; it needs endorsements from three members of the same category, a resume and biography, and notarisation, and the category Council approves it.
The DGA initiation fee from July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027 is $15,703 for a feature or television director and $5,000 for a commercial, documentary, low-budget feature, staff or segment director.
A director joining on a low-budget (under $11 million) narrative or documentary feature pays 40% of the $5,000 fee up front and the rest over a year.
The Assistant Directors Training Program (Los Angeles) requires US work eligibility, a high school diploma or GED, and a degree, E-5 military rank, or two years (520 workdays) of paid work.
The New York training program takes 5 to 7 trainees from 300 to 350 applications a year, charges no application fee, and its 2027 application closes December 1, 2026.
Sundance's Screenwriters Lab takes first- or second-time fiction feature writer-directors; the Directors Lab has no open application and draws on projects already supported by the Institute.
Applications for Sundance's 2027 Screenwriters Lab and Intensive ran April 14 to May 12, 2026, with about 1,000 to 1,200 screenplays in the second round, and only an application fee is charged.
The Sundance Directors Lab for 2027 runs May 3-18, 2027 in Sundance, Utah.

The DGA minimum for a high-budget theatrical feature director is $25,214 a week, with a 10-week guaranteed employment period, 2 weeks of preparation and 1 week of cutting allowance (July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027).

Under the Low Budget Sideletter a theatrical director's pay is negotiable up to $3 million; it is at least $8,321 a week (33% of scale) from $3 to $4 million, $18,911 (75%) from $4 to $8.5 million and $22,693 (90%) from $8.5 to $11 million.

Network prime-time episode minimums are $34,629 (half hour), $58,808 (one hour), $98,018 (90 minutes) and $164,661 (two hours); non-network non-prime-time minimums are $15,558, $31,106, $46,672 and $64,983.

Network prime-time pilot minimums are $98,018 (half hour) with 14 included days, $130,683 (one hour) with 24, $163,343 (90 minutes) with 34 and $228,695 (two hours) with 50; the first episode of a series ordered without a pilot pays 150% of the episode rate.

High-budget SVOD minimums on services with 20 million or more subscribers run from $19,636 (20-35 minutes, budget $1.03-2.1M) to $70,616 (36-65 minutes, budget $7M or more) per episode, and $111,598 or $164,755 for a feature of 96 minutes or more.
Soft-prep: a director working non-exclusively on a theatrical film before official pre-production is paid $5,000 a week up to $50,000 when 3 of 4 named crew are employed weekly.
A seventh day in a workweek or a listed holiday pays 1/5 of weekly salary plus $4,523.
Theatrical films released in supplemental markets other than cassettes pay 1.2% of the employer's accountable receipts, half to the director and a third to the DGA pension plan.
On cassettes/home video the director receives 1% of employer's gross up to $1,000,000 and 1.2% above it.

Network prime-time dramatic rerun residuals per run were $13,254 (half hour), $24,963 (one hour), $37,436 (90 minutes) and $49,443 (two hours) for 2023-26, and the 2026 agreement keeps them at those rates.
The 2026 agreement raises minimum salaries by 2.5% at its start (July 1, 2026), then 3% on July 1, 2027, 2028 and 2029, compounded.

US Producers and Directors (OEWS 27-2012) earned a median $90,360 in 2025, with the 10th percentile at $45,780 and the 90th at $198,540; in Los Angeles the median was $131,600 and the 90th percentile $325,310.
In the New York metro area the 2025 median for Producers and Directors was $108,460.
Weekly AD/UPM minimums (studio) are $7,197 for a UPM, $6,843 for a First AD, $4,585 for a Key Second AD and $4,329 for a 2nd Second AD.
New York AD trainees earn $1,085 a week in their first quarter rising to $1,333 in the fourth, with overtime after 54 hours.
The DGA is the sole bargaining agent for directors, UPMs, ADs and associate directors with the AMPTP employers, and every covered employee must be or become a member in good standing.
The 2026 Basic Agreement and FLTTA run four years, from July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2030; members ratified them on June 26, 2026.
DGA dues are $62.50 a quarter plus 1.6% of gross earnings between $10,000 and $825,000 a year, plus 1% of residuals.
A member who later works in a higher category pays the difference in initiation fees, and an upgrade needs the right qualification list placement.
Employers contribute 8.75% to the DGA pension plan and 13.5% to the health plan on a director's salary, and the director contributes 2.5% to the pension plan.
On a theatrical film the pension contribution ceiling is $300,000 and the health ceiling $520,000.
A DGA member must work under a DGA contract even on a low- or no-budget feature, documentary or new-media project.
The Stage Directors and Choreographers Society charges a full member $2,400 initiation and $240 a year; an associate member pays $375 and $90.
The director's credit is "Directed by" on screen and in paid advertising, and no one but a director may be given a credit using the word "Director" or "Direction".
Only one director is assigned to a motion picture at a time, except bona fide teams, segments, second units and similar practices; a Guild waiver is possible for two directors.
On a theatrical film the director's screen credit stands alone on the last title card before principal photography, and in paid ads it is at least 15% of the title's type size.
When more than one director worked, the Guild decides the credit; if it does not decide within 14 days (theatrical) or 7 days (television), the employer decides.

No possessive credit ("A Film by") may go to a director on a first feature unless the director brought the property to the employer and did substantial development work; Sideletter 27 also deleted the automatic "A Film By" on ads with six or more credits.
A hyphenated credit such as "Produced and Written by" counts as separate credits for the advertising rules.

The DGA Theatrical Feature Film award is open to DGA and non-DGA directors of a film over 40 minutes released for at least seven consecutive days in a paid theater in Los Angeles or New York in 2026; day-and-date releases are not eligible.
The director must have exercised all directorial functions in original photography and have an on-screen "Directed By" credit; DGA members vote, the top five become nominees on January 7, 2027.
The 79th DGA Awards take place on January 30, 2027; first-time feature entries for the Michael Apted Award are due October 16, 2026.
Academy Directors Branch members nominate up to five films for Directing, and active and life members vote the final round.
Oscar eligibility needs a qualifying run of at least seven consecutive days in a commercial theater in one of six US metro areas, beginning in calendar 2026 for the 99th Awards.
The DGA Student Spotlight Awards give $2,500 to winning student directors from marginalized communities.
A director who also works as a producer or writer stays classified as a director for the directing work.
Under the WGA, anyone credited as a producer in any capacity or as the director is a "production executive" for writing credit.
A production executive who is a later writer on an original screenplay needs more than 50% of the final shooting script for credit, and any writer needs more than 33% on a non-original screenplay.
Any screen credit proposed for a production executive who did not write alone goes to automatic credit arbitration.
When an episode's director is also employed on the series as producer-director, no intervening-day payments are owed for a hiatus.
A UPM also employed as producer on a theatrical film has pension and health contributions made on at least $150,000 for pictures starting on or after July 1, 2026.
In 2020-21, 64% of first-time episodic directing jobs went to people affiliated with the show, mostly writer-producers and actors.
Sundance's Screenwriters Lab and Intensive admit writer-directors and writer-director teams.

topics.topic: Time and money of a project

facts.fact: The Director's Cut of a theatrical film is due within 10 weeks of the close of principal photography or one editing day per two scheduled shooting days, whichever is greater; six weeks on a low-budget film.
On television the Director's Cut is one day plus up to one more for 30 minutes and four days for 60 minutes; a high-budget SVOD feature of $22.5 million or more gets 10 weeks.
A one-hour network prime-time episode guarantees 7 preparation days and 8 shooting days; a two-hour one guarantees 15 and 27.
A director who replaces another for reasons other than incapacity is guaranteed only the rest of the previous guarantee, at double minimum.
On a $40 million-plus theatrical film a director earning under 150% of scale is paid $5,000 a week for full-time post more than 9 months after the Director's Cut, up to $50,000.
DGA-covered theatrical releases fell from 292 in 2018 to 162 in 2022.
The Los Angeles AD trainee works a typical day of 12 to 16 hours.
Women directed 37% of 1,430 DGA-covered episodes in the 2023-24 season, up from 16% ten years before.
Women held 41% of full-season directorial-team jobs in 2023-24: 31% of First ADs, 51% of Second ADs and 43% of UPMs.
Women directed 16% of DGA-covered feature releases in 2018-2022 (12% in 2018, 22% in 2020), 13% of high-budget and 18% of low-budget releases.
Women directed 27% of the 382 first DGA-covered features of 2018-2022.
Women got 46% of first-time episodic directing jobs in the 2020-21 season.
The New York AD Training Program requires applicants to be at least 21 by the June start.
California regulates contracts by unemancipated minors for artistic services, including as a director, writer or producer (Family Code 6750).
A court approving such a contract requires 15% of the minor's gross earnings to be set aside in trust, blocked until 18 or emancipation (Family Code 6752).
The DGA Student Spotlight Awards require the director to identify as from a marginalized community and be a current or recent student.
Sundance's Screenwriters Intensive gives priority to artists from traditionally underrepresented communities.

sources.title: Directors Guild of America Basic Agreement of 2023 (term July 1, 2023 to June 30, 2026; carried into the 2026 BA by the 2026 MOA)
sources.said: The Guild is recognized by the Employer as the sole collective bargaining agent for all Directors, Unit Production Managers, Assistant Directors and Associate Directors in the motion picture industry ... A Director is one who directs the production of motion pictures, as the word "direct" is commonly used in the motion picture industry. ... The fact that the Director may also render services as a Producer and/or Writer or in any other capacity shall not take the individual out of the classification as a Director ... each Employee employed by the Employer shall be or become a member of the Guild in good standing ... There will be only one Director assigned to direct a motion picture at any given time. ... the Employer may assign another Director to function as a consultant (herein called "Consulting Director") ... is not entitled to credit under Article 8 or any creative rights under Article 7. ... the substituting Director shall only be guaranteed the unexpired portion of the previous Director's guarantee, at not less than double minimum compensation for the work performed. ... The Director shall prepare the Director's Cut of the film for presentation to the individual Producer and to the person designated in the Director's deal memo as having final cutting authority ... Within ten (10) weeks after the close of principal photography or within a period of time after the close of principal photography equal to one (1) day of editing time for each two (2) days of originally scheduled photography ... within six (6) weeks after the close of principal photography ... As to television motion pictures having a running time of thirty (30) minutes or less, within one (1) day plus time and the opportunity to make changes, if necessary, but not to exceed one (1) more day. ... As to television motion pictures having a running time of sixty (60) minutes or less, but more than thirty (30) minutes, within four (4) days. ... If the Guild should fail to reach a decision and notify the Employer within fourteen (14) days in the case of a theatrical motion picture, and seven (7) days in the case of a television motion picture ... The form of the Director's credit on screen, paid advertising, phonograph records, books, tapes, videodiscs, videocassettes and the containers thereof, when and as required, shall be "Directed by...." ... Employer will not grant to any individual, other than a Director, any credit which includes the word "Director," "Direction" or any derivation thereof. ... No other credit shall appear on the card which accords credit to the Director of the film. ... Such credit shall be on the last title card appearing prior to principal photography. ... the size of type of the Director's credit shall be no less than fifteen percent (15%) of the size of type used for the title of the motion picture ... the Director shall also be accorded an additional credit above the title in the form "A Film By" ... Hyphenated credits (e.g., "Produced and Written by...") count as separate credits. ... Re: Possessive Credit ... any non-series television motion picture (90) minutes or longer ... The Directors' Council of the Guild shall not unreasonably withhold its consent to a waiver of the above provisions when two (2) Directors apply for the same based on professional necessity. ... the Director has not previously directed a motion picture under this or any preceding BA ... at least seventy-five percent (75%) must be spent with the actual shooting company ... no possessive credit in any form may be accorded to a Director on his or her first feature film, unless the Director was responsible for bringing to the Employer the literary property upon which the film is based and the Director performed substantial services in development of the property. ... The following sentence in BA §8-203(d) is deleted: ... the Director is also employed on the series in another capacity (e.g., a Producer-Director, Director of Photography) ... Employer shall pay additional compensation of one and two-tenths percent (1.2%) of the Employer's accountable receipts from the distribution of Such Picture. ... one-half (½) of such amount to be paid to the Director; one-third (⅓) of such amount to be paid to the Directors Guild of America – Producer Pension Plan ... Until the Employer's gross equals $1,000,000, 1% thereof shall be paid to the Director ... After the Employer's gross exceeds $1,000,000, 1.2% thereof shall be paid to the Director ... ½ hour $13,254 1 hour $24,963 1½ hours $37,436 2 hours* $49,443 ... Any individual who has been employed four hundred (400) days in work as a Second Assistant Director, First Assistant Director, Unit Production Manager or Associate Director ... a Trainee or Intern must complete four hundred (400) days of on-the-job training ... has completed at least five hundred twenty (520) working days as a Second Assistant Director ... completed at least two hundred sixty (260) working days as a First Assistant Director ... The Director shall have the right, subject to the terms of Articles 14 and 15, to select the First Assistant Director on any theatrical motion picture ... the Director shall see the dailies of each day's photography at a reasonable time.

sources.said: A Reminder List of all eligible motion pictures shall be made available along with a nominations ballot to all members of the Directors Branch, who shall vote in the order of their preference for not more than five productions. ... Final voting for the Directing award shall be restricted to active and life Academy members. ... in one of the six qualifying U.S. metro areas ... for a theatrical qualifying run of at least seven consecutive days in the same commercial motion picture theater ... must begin between January 1, 2026, and December 31, 2026.

sources.title: Sundance Institute, 2027 Development Track FAQ
sources.said: The Screenwriters Lab is for first- or second-time fiction feature writers, writer-directors, or writer-director teams. ... The Screenwriters Intensive is for first-time fiction feature writers or writer-directors, with priority given to artists from traditionally underrepresented communities. ... There is no open application process for the Directors Lab, which is typically populated by projects that have already been supported via a prior Institute program, such as a Screenwriters Lab, Intensive, or grant. ... Applications for the 2027 Screenwriters Lab and Screenwriters Intensive will be available online from April 14, 2026, through May 12, 2026 ... Approximately 1,000 to 1,200 complete screenplays are considered as part of the second round. ... Aside from an application fee, we do not charge for participation in our programs.

sources.title: Stage Directors and Choreographers Society, Prospective Member FAQs
sources.said: SDC is a national labor union and at this time covers stage work in the United States only. ... To join as a Full Member , initiation is currently $2,400 and Annual Dues are currently $240. ... To join as an Associate Member , initiation is currently $375 and Annual Dues are currently $90.

sources.title: California Senate Judiciary Committee, analysis of SB 764 (hearing January 11, 2024), "Existing law" on Family Code 6750-6753
sources.said: Regulates the following contracts entered into between an unemancipated minor and a third party: ... writer, director, producer, production executive, choreographer, ... Requires the court, in an order approving the above contracts, to require that 15 percent of the minor’s gross earnings pursuant to the contract be set aside by the minor’s employer ... blocked from use until the minor is emancipated or reaches age 18. ... (Fam. Code § 6750.) ... (Fam. Code § 6752.)

note:
Director (film and television, US depth; theatre directing through the SDC where it bears on the screen career). Read 2026-10-31. Documents and their dates in force: the DGA Minimum Salary Schedule for July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027 (revised 9/23/26; its Low Budget Sideletter page says those rates remain tentative); the DGA Basic Agreement of 2023 (term July 1, 2023 to June 30, 2026), whose text the 2026 Memorandum of Agreement (June 9, 2026) carries into the 2026 BA except as amended; the 2026 MOA is a scanned PDF with no text layer and was read by eye (pages 1-2 only: term and wage increases; the rest of its 68 pages, including any change to creative rights, credits, residual formulas or the health plan, was not read); DGA press release of June 26, 2026 (ratification); DGA Membership (Joining the DGA and Upgrades views, rendered honestly with Playwright because the page holds them in script and shows one per menu choice; initiation fees for July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027); DGA Dues page (undated, current site); DGA Independent Directors Committee FAQ (undated and older: it gives dues of $50 a quarter and 1.5% to $300,000, and a level table with Level 3 at $2.6-3.75M, which the Dues page and the 2026 rate card supersede; only its joining routes, low-budget fee terms and the coverage rule are used); LA ADTP 2025 Application Instructions (its trainee wage scale is as of July 1, 2022, not used); NY ADTP apply and FAQ pages (2027 cycle); WGA Screen Credits Manual (current web version); DGA inclusion releases of October 25, 2024 (TV 2023-24), May 5, 2022 (TV 2020-21, first-time directors) and December 21, 2023 (features 2018-2022); O*NET OnLine 27-2012.02 summary and 27-2012.00 local wages (BLS 2025 OEWS data, employment 2025, projections 2025-2035); DGA Awards 79th rules and schedule; DGA Student Spotlight 2027 rules; Academy 99th Awards complete rules (May 2026); Sundance 2027 Development Track FAQ and Feature Film Program page; SDC Prospective Member FAQs (undated).
Readings made: the pay tiers by budget are the rate card's Low Budget Sideletter page (Levels 1-2 to $3M negotiable; Level 3 to $4M at 33%; Levels 4A-4B to $8.5M at 75%; Level 4C to $11M at 90%). 'Directed by' and the one-director rule are BA 8-102, 8-103(b) and 7-208. The possessive-credit rule is Sideletter No. 27. Residual splits are BA 18-103 and 18-104. The QL day counts are BA 14-302 to 14-304 (Southern California). The 2025 OEWS figures are for the combined occupation Producers and Directors (27-2012), as O*NET publishes them; directors alone are not separated. The O*NET employment (181,000) and projected openings (12,100) are on the 27-2012.02 page and belong to the occupation O*NET shows there. The 64% affiliated first-break share is the 2020-21 season's; no later first-time figure was found on dga.org.
Not found or not read: the DGA-Producer Health Plan's current minimum earnings for eligibility and the Pension Plan's vesting rules (dgaplans.org answered with an Incapsula check; not passed; dga.org pages found give only a 2008 figure, not used); the BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook page and the OEWS 27-2012 page (bls.gov refused with Akamai 403; archive.org snapshots exist, 2026-10-21 for the OOH page, but web.archive.org reset every connection today, so O*NET's copy of the BLS 2025 data is used); the California Family Code text itself (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov answered with a Cloudflare challenge; archive reset), so sections 6750 and 6752 are cited from the California Senate Judiciary Committee's January 2024 analysis of SB 764 as secondary, and 6751 (court approval, venue) and 6753 were not read in their own words; the age at which a minor may join the DGA (no DGA page found states one); a DGA strike history (the DGA reached and ratified the 2026 deal without a strike; no strike page read); director agents and managers (California Talent Agencies Act licensing and commission rules were not researched in this pass); the Michael Apted first-time award's eligibility rules (only its deadline and ceremony dates were read); the Television Academy's directing Emmy rules; DGA commercial and FLTTA minimums beyond those on the BA rate card; SDC contract minimums (Broadway and others were not read). No award read here is split by sex; the Academy's Directing rule and the DGA feature rules name no sex or age condition (a reading of their texts).
